title: 2021 HMMT November Guts Problem 8
statement: Let \(p, q, r\) be primes such that \(2 p+3 q=6 r\). Find \(p+q+r\).

solutions.text: First, it is known that \(3 q=6 r-2 p=2(3 r-p)\), thus \(q\) is even. The only even prime is 2 so \(q=2\). Further, \(2 p=6 r-3 q=3(2 r-q)\), which means that \(p\) is a multiple of 3 and thus \(p=3\). This means that \(2 \cdot 3+3 \cdot 2=6 r \Longrightarrow r=2\). Therefore, \(p+q+r=3+2+2=7\).
